title: Fix Jobs detail/logs read-surface metadata to derive availability from canonical owner result

frozen_hosted_evidence_boundary.note: This task is source-only and hosted unverified. Frozen hosted evidence Root39158664258 (commit bd85e11cd2c7f47b78a8a14e23ee5c0b593d3c21) predates this change and does not include this fix; a subsequent governed dev release and smoke run are required before claiming hosted closure.

summary.problem: GET /bff/jobs/{job_id} and GET /bff/jobs/{job_id}/logs resolved job detail/logs through JobReadPort (setting job['source'] to the canonical owner, e.g. 'training_session'), but computed response metadata via read_surface_meta('jobs', 'job_detail' | 'job_logs', snapshot_at=snapshot_at) without passing the owner surface, falling back to ReadSurfacePorts.dataset_source('jobs') == 'missing' and reporting meta.surfaces.job_detail/job_logs as {'status': 'unavailable', 'source': 'missing'} with degradation. Additionally, get_job's 'if not job:' branch checked dataset_surface_status('jobs') and called raise_if_read_surface_unavailable, turning genuine owner 404 responses into 503 when dataset_source('jobs') was 'missing'.
summary.solution: Added _owner_job_meta inside create_jobs_router in services/control-plane/bff/jobs/router.py to derive surface status and source from the canonical owner job returned by _lookup_job(job_id) via existing dataset_surface_status and read_surface_meta interfaces, and removed the legacy 'jobs' dataset availability check from the 'if not job:' branch of get_job since _lookup_job(job_id) already maps JobSourceUnavailableError to HTTP 503.

verified_invariants: GET /bff/jobs/{job_id} returns HTTP 200 with meta.surfaces.job_detail == {'status': 'ok', 'source': <canonical_owner>} and no meta.degradation when the canonical owner returns a job, even when store.dataset_source('jobs') == 'missing'.

GET /bff/jobs/{job_id}/logs returns HTTP 200 with meta.surfaces.job_logs == {'status': 'ok', 'source': <canonical_owner>} and no meta.degradation when the canonical owner returns a job, even when store.dataset_source('jobs') == 'missing'.
Missing job from canonical owner or unrecognized job_id prefix returns HTTP 404 (RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND), never 503, even when store.dataset_source('jobs') == 'missing'.
Unavailable canonical owner raises JobSourceUnavailableError and returns HTTP 503 (DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE).
Request-scoped caller Authorization and verified X-Tenant-Id forwarding, tenant isolation, and all six canonical job source projections remain intact.
